description: Deep purple veined in gold, heavy as a crown. Unclaimed, which has not stopped anyone hunting for it.
lore: The names a bench uses for what a stone grades to are all borrowed from creatures: frost, ember, storm, grave, blood, moss. Point at the word and you can point at the animal. This one is filed royal, and royal is not a kind of anything — it is the word that got used because the tray needed a word. There is no creature anybody would file under it, which has not stopped two or three crews going out to look, with no description to go on and a price to go on instead.

It does not cut. It does not burn and it will not hold anyone up. What it does is get you paid: an offer arrives a tenth over what the same bench would have said an hour before, and the man making it cannot afterwards say why, and ground you have walked twice gives up [[lore/the_gold_agreement|gold]] on the third pass. Nearly everything else on the shelf is an appetite or an endurance. Pressed to the bottom of this one is an expectation of being owed.

Deep purple plates, thick gold in the seams, and heavy — nothing that size has any business sitting in a hand like that. Two hundred and seventy-five gold, a number arrived at by merchants, in a room, with one of these on the table. Twice a year somebody proposes a blind price: the stone in a box, in another room, valued by people who cannot see it. The proposal has never once been carried, and the men who vote it down are the men holding one.
gm_notes: Unbound, handled as a taxonomy problem rather than a mystery: 'royal' is the one nature on the benches with nothing under it, and the record proposes no candidate. The blind-price vote is the payload and doubles as an in-world account of the item's own 275 — the stone had a hand in its price. Items line adopted verbatim.
